dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Owen. How can I help you?
Hi, um, yeah, hi. So I'm trying to figure out about a permit? Like, I think it's ready to pick up, but I'm not totally sure?
Okay. Let's take it one step at a time. Do you know what kind of permit it is?
It's, um, for work on the house. I got an email, or I think it was an email, that said something was approved? And I was like, okay, so do I go get it or does it come in the mail?

Alright. Building permits are usually handled at the permit counter rather than through our desk here, but I can tell you how that generally works. Do you have a permit number or an application number from the email?
Hang on, let me look. I'm in the car, sorry. Okay, it says application, and then a bunch of numbers, and then there's another number that says reference? Which one do you need?
Let's start with the one that says application. Read it to me slowly, and I'll repeat it back.
Okay, so it's, um, hold on, the screen keeps dimming. Okay. It's four, four, one, seven.
Four, four, one, seven. Is that the whole number, or are there more digits after that?
Oh. No, there's a dash and then like two, two? So four four one seven, dash, two two?

Got it. Four four one seven, dash two two. Honestly, I can't pull up the details of that from this desk, and I wouldn't want to tell you it's ready when I can't see it. The permit counter can confirm. Would you like me to transfer you?
Um, well, actually, what I really wanted to know is what time they close? Because I'm going to be driving back through on the way home, and I thought I could just stop and grab it?
Sure, that I can help with. City Hall is open weekdays, and the permit counter generally closes a little before the end of the afternoon. I'd say plan to be there before four to be safe.
Before four. Okay. So like, three thirty is fine? Or is that cutting it close?
Three thirty should be fine. Earlier is better, though, in case there's a line.
Okay, totally. And what about you guys? Like, this office, your hours? Are they the same? Because I thought maybe I'd have to come to you first?

Good question. Our office keeps regular weekday business hours, roughly eight thirty to four thirty. You wouldn't have to come to us first for a building permit, though. You'd go straight to the permit counter.
Wait, so eight thirty to four thirty for you, but the permit counter is before four? Why are they different?
Different counters can wrap up at different times. The permit counter tends to stop taking people a bit earlier so they can finish what's in front of them. It's a bit confusing, I know.
Okay, okay. So, um, it's like, you're open later but they're the ones I need? Which is kind of backwards? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult.
Not difficult at all. Yes, that's right. I'm open a little later, but the permit counter is the one you need, so aim for before four.
Got it. Okay. And do I need to bring anything? Like ID, or the email, or the paper application? I didn't keep the paper one, I think my contractor has it?

I'd bring a photo ID and either print the email or have it up on your phone. Beyond that, the permit counter would know exactly what they need. If you like, I can transfer you now and you can ask them directly.
Um, yeah, maybe? Actually, wait. Is it for my address that they look it up? Or is it the contractor's name? I'm on Coggeshall, three eighty-two, if that helps?
Three eighty-two Coggeshall Avenue. They'll most likely look it up by the application number or the address, so you've got both. The contractor's name might help as well, if you have it.

Okay, I have that, it's on the email too. Oh my gosh, I'm sorry, I'm all over the place. You're, like, really easy to understand, by the way? You talk so clearly. Most people I call, I'm like, what? But you, I totally got everything.
Well, thank you, that's kind of you to say. I try to go slowly so nothing gets missed.
No, it works. Okay, so, yes, transfer me? And if it doesn't go through, I'll just go there at like three?
That sounds like a good plan. Let me connect you. If the line drops, call back and ask for the permit counter, and I'll try again.
Okay, thank you so much. Bye.
You're welcome. Hold on just a moment while I transfer you.
